chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Abū Wallād, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Those to whom We have given the Book recite it as it ought to be recited; they are the ones who believe in it.
He عليه السلام said: They are the Imams عليهم السلام.

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, identified here as the intended referents of the verse
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the revealed Book, referring here to divine scripture
key_terms.حَقَّ تِلَاوَتِهِ: its true recital, reciting it as is truly due
key_terms.يَتْلُونَهُ: they recite it, meaning they read and convey it properly
key_terms.يُؤْمِنُونَ بِهِ: they believe in it with true faith

ai.seo_question: Who are those who recite the Book as it ought to be recited in Qur'an 2:121?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic verse by identifying those who truly recite the Book as the Imams عليهم السلام. It presents the Imams as the ones who embody true faith in and proper recitation of the divine scripture.
